//: PROVENANCE AS A BUILD INPUT — SA §TS-12.3/§TS-12.4, SD §FE-10, SD Revision Log D8. One record per safety_critical key PER LOCALE. `content_hash` is `sha256:` + lowercase hex SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the catalogue source string after Unicode NFC normalisation; `contentHash()` in src/review.ts is the one implementation and gate:safety-review-currency (T-044) must use it rather than re-deriving it. The gate's rule: for every safety_critical key and every enabled locale, FAIL unless a record exists here whose content_hash equals the current source's hash, whose status is `signed_off`, whose provenance is not `placeholder`, and which names a reviewer and a review date — UNLESS the key is inside an unexpired `pending_pipeline` waiver. Editing a safety string changes its hash and therefore un-signs it; that is the mechanism, not a side effect. An MT engine cannot produce a record here, which is what makes DV-11's ban on machine-translating safety copy enforceable rather than intended. T-233 (OE-66/OE-67/OE-68, EV-16): a record may name an AI MODEL as `authored_by`, with `provenance: "ai_authored"`, ONLY when it cites a stakeholder ruling in `ruling` that makes that model the author of that locale's copy (OE-66: el, ru; OE-67: en safety_critical). The rulings and the model identity they name are written in src/pipeline.test.ts as a literal, not here — a register that could grant its own authorship authority would be measuring itself. An `ai_authored` record is AUTHORED, never REVIEWED: sign-off still requires the named, stakeholder-confirmed human DSL or deputy in `reviewed_by`, and no record here is signed off.

pending_pipeline.expected_by_means: A DECISION REVIEW DATE, not a delivery date, and the distinction is the point. Nobody has promised safety copy by this date — no external engagement has begun, so there is nothing to promise. What must happen by it is a DECISION: either a real `external_start` is recorded and this date is re-anchored to start + the 42-day lead time, or it is re-anchored again with a stated reason and a new `re_anchors` row. The gate behaviour is unchanged and the self-closing property is unchanged: after this date gate:safety-review-currency (T-044) fails the build on these keys exactly as on unwaived ones. This is NOT an open-ended waiver and must not become one — see `re_anchors` and the bound asserted in src/pipeline.test.ts.
pending_pipeline.external_start_note: Recorded explicitly as null so the absence is DATA rather than a missing field: a null that means 'has not happened' is checkable, an absent key is ambiguous. The single source of truth is `pipeline.external_start`, which this mirrors and which `loadCopyPipeline()` refuses to load without. Set on the day the brief is actually delivered to a named practitioner, by the stakeholder, and by nobody else.
pending_pipeline.owner: frontend-developer (T-049) — Greek-authoring safeguarding practitioner + briefed Russian translator + DSL sign-off
pending_pipeline.reason: SD §DH-5 external dependency 2: the trilingual safety-copy pipeline has a six-week external lead time and no engineering dependency beyond T-040. Until T-233 the catalogue strings these keys held were ENGINEERING PLACEHOLDERS written by T-040 to exercise the compile, gate and render mechanisms. Since T-233 they hold copy AUTHORED BY AN AI MODEL under stakeholder rulings OE-66/OE-67 (EV-16) — authored, NOT reviewed: no DSL or deputy is named and nothing is signed off, so it is still not reviewed safety copy and must not ship. This waiver is dated and self-closing: after `expected_by` the gate fails on these keys exactly as it would on unwaived ones. That is BOARD RK-2's standing escalation with a date on it instead of a reminder.

re_anchors.decided_by: stakeholder, via the orchestrator (escalation OE-5, raised from T-049 OD-15)
re_anchors.note: T-040 set expected_by = opened_at + six weeks because SD §DH-5 says six weeks, not because a clock had started. Measured in T-049: 2026-09-05 → 2026-10-17 is exactly 42 days, identical to the stated external lead time, so the latest workable external start was the day the waiver opened and slack was zero on arrival. 2026-10-17 was therefore never a forecast. Re-anchored honestly rather than allowed to expire into a build failure whose cheapest repair is deleting the waiver. THE CHAIN IS THE POINT: a date edited without a row here is caught, because the last `to` must equal `expected_by`.

pending_pipeline.re_anchors_note: Append-only. Each row's `from` must equal the previous row's `to`, the first row's `from` is the original 2026-10-17, and the last row's `to` must equal `expected_by` — so moving the date without recording why is a red test, not a quiet edit. RE-ANCHORS MADE WHILE `external_start` IS NULL ARE BOUNDED, and the bound is a literal in src/pipeline.test.ts rather than a field here: a register that could raise its own limit would be measuring itself. Exceeding it is an orchestrator decision against BOARD RK-2 and must cost an edit to that line.

pipeline.//: THE PIPELINE ITSELF, as data rather than as a plan in someone's head — T-049, SD §DH-5 external dependency 2, SA §TS-12.4. `entries` above records what HAS been reviewed; this block records what MUST happen, by whom, in which language, and by when, so that the six-week lead time can be MEASURED against a date instead of remembered. Nothing here asserts that any copy has been authored, translated or reviewed. Every `named` and every `completed_at` is null, and that is the honest state on 2026-09-05. T-233 amendment (2026-09-28): the stakeholder rulings OE-66 (el/ru, 2026-09-27T18:54:51Z) and OE-67 (en safety_critical, 2026-09-27T19:27:39Z) made an AI model (Claude Opus) the AUTHOR of the current copy in place of the practitioner and translator this plan names. `entries` now records that truthfully (`ai_authored`, the model as `authored_by`, the ruling cited). The authoring roles and stages below are left as they were — they describe the human path, which the rulings displaced for this copy but did not abolish — and are still null because none of those humans exists. The DSL and deputy review is UNCHANGED by either ruling: still human, still unnamed, still the only route to `signed_off`.
pipeline.external_start_note: The date the brief below actually reaches a named Greek-authoring safeguarding practitioner. Only a stakeholder can set this, because only a stakeholder can engage the two people. It is null because it has not happened — an undated start cannot be measured against a lead time, and a start date recorded before the fact would be the exact defect this register exists to prevent.
pipeline.lead_time_source: SD §DH-5 external dependency 2: "Six weeks of lead time on a path that has no engineering dependency and therefore gets scheduled last by default."
pipeline.deadline_source: pending_pipeline.expected_by — the self-closing waiver above, re-anchored once on 2026-09-05 (see pending_pipeline.re_anchors). It is a DECISION REVIEW DATE, not a delivery date. After it, gate:safety-review-currency (T-044) fails the build on these keys exactly as on unwaived ones. Moving it again means appending a re_anchors row AND moving the literal in src/pipeline.test.ts, together.
pipeline.latest_external_start_note: deadline minus lead_time_days. DERIVED, and asserted in src/pipeline.test.ts against those two values written there as literals — so buying slack by editing this field turns the suite red. On the ORIGINAL 2026-10-17 anchor this fell on 2026-09-05, the very day the pipeline was opened: the waiver window and the lead time were the same six weeks and there was no slack at all (decisions.md OD-15, escalated as OE-5). The re-anchor to 2026-12-05 buys back a real 42-day window; it does not start it. Nothing starts until `external_start` is non-null.
pipeline.blocked_on_note: Not blocked on engineering. Every mechanism this pipeline needs — the register, the hash, the compiler refusals, the waiver, the gate T-044 will build over it — exists. What does not exist is a safeguarding practitioner and a translator, and no agent in this programme can engage either. See packages/i18n/PIPELINE.md §5.

greek_authoring_safeguarding_practitione.what: Authors the English and Greek safety copy IN PARALLEL — not English first and Greek after. Must be a safeguarding practitioner working in Cyprus, because the copy encodes the Cyprus reporting pathway (112, 1466, 116 111, 199, Social Welfare Services) and not a UK one.

russian_translator_briefed.what: Professional translator, briefed on the safeguarding context BEFORE translating. The brief is a separate deliverable and a separate stage precisely because it is the step that gets skipped.

dsl.what: Designated Safeguarding Lead. Signs off PER LOCALE and is the only role whose name may appear in `reviewed_by`. The DSL and deputy BETWEEN THEM must cover English, Greek and Russian — a DSL who cannot read Russian cannot sign off Russian copy, and the deputy is how that is covered.
dsl.spec: PM §MVP-L5 AC7; SA §TS-12.4; SD Revision Log D8

dsl_deputy.what: Deputy DSL. Also permitted in `reviewed_by`. Exists in this roster because §MVP-L5 AC7 makes trilingual coverage a property of the PAIR, not of one person.

stages.what: English and Greek authored in parallel. NOT English-then-translate.
stages.output: Catalogue values for en and el; provenance `authored`.

stages.what: The safeguarding-context brief is delivered to and acknowledged by the translator, before any translation begins.
stages.output: A dated acknowledgement. Recorded here as the stage `completed_at`.

stages.what: Russian produced by the briefed human translator. Machine translation is prohibited at this tier (DV-11) and cannot produce a record in `entries` at all.

DSL review and sign-off, PER LOCALE. This is the step that writes `entries[<locale>][<key>]` with a real `reviewed_by` and `reviewed_at`, and it is the only step that can make gate:safety-review-currency pass.
In-context review in the running product at the target locale, on a 360 px Android viewport. A string that is correct and overflows its container is a failed safety string.
stages.output: Screenshots per locale. Needs T-050/T-051 surfaces to exist; until then this stage cannot complete, and it must not be recorded as though it had.

stages.what: Read-aloud pass. Copy that scans well on screen frequently does not survive being spoken — which is why SA §INT-5r specifies PRE-RECORDED audio per locale rather than runtime TTS (DV-7).
stages.output: A dated read-aloud confirmation per locale for the affected keys.

safety.emergency.address_prompt.channel_note: The user reads this ALOUD to a 112 operator while an emergency is in progress. It must survive being spoken by a frightened person, not merely read on a screen — SA §TS-12.4 read-aloud pass.

en.why: Source authorship. SA §TS-12.4: English and Greek are authored IN PARALLEL by the safeguarding author.

el.why: MUST be natively authored, never translated from English. PM §MVP-L4 AC4 and §MVP-S7 AC1 both require Greek AUTHORSHIP. A Greek translation of an English safety string is a different artefact from a Greek safety string and this field is where the difference is enforced rather than hoped for.

ru.why: Professional translator BRIEFED ON THE SAFEGUARDING CONTEXT (PM §MVP-L4 AC4). SA §TS-12.4: a translator who does not know a string is an escalation message will produce a grammatically perfect, operationally useless one. Machine translation is prohibited outright at this tier (DV-11) and the brief is a required, separately-recorded stage.
